# Rishabh Thakur

> Electrical Engineering and Computer Science undergraduate at UC Berkeley. Research interests include robotics, robot learning, reinforcement learning, and autonomous systems. Currently working on decentralized multi-agent robot learning at ICON Lab and Berkeley AI Research, advised by Professor Negar Mehr and Dayi Ethan Dong. Previously a research intern at UPenn's GRASP Lab and UC Santa Cruz, and software captain of Innov8rz, FIRST Tech Challenge Team 11039.

This is Rishabh Thakur's personal website. It contains an about page, coursework, past work with an interactive robot CAD model, and technical notes on robot learning and optimization. This file is an author-provided overview with direct links to the published material. The Past Work page is still being updated and is not a complete record of his projects.

## Research and experience

- UC Berkeley ICON Lab / Berkeley AI Research: undergraduate research on decentralized multi-agent robot learning. The project studies how robots can coordinate using local observations and pretrained single-agent skills. Current interests include lightweight coordination heads, skill composition, timing, and residual adaptation of diffusion policies.
- University of Pennsylvania GRASP Lab: research internship involving autonomous-vehicle safety, vehicle tracking, and collision detection, using OpenCV, ROS, and Kalman filtering.
- UC Santa Cruz AIEA Lab: research internship involving autonomous-driving perception, visual odometry, and detecting adversarial tampering in camera data.
- Innov8rz, FTC Team 11039: former software captain, with experience in competition robotics, robot control, and working across software, mechanical, and electrical systems.

## Projects and media

- [Cupid project and interactive viewer, HTML](https://rishabht.com/past-work/): FTC robot for the 2025-26 season. Rotate, zoom, and pan the CAD assembly in the browser.
- [Cupid 3D CAD assembly, glTF binary](https://rishabht.com/past-work/assets/cupid-final.glb): the model used by the site's interactive viewer.

## Technical notes

- [Residual Denoising vs. Action-Space Residuals in Diffusion Policies](https://rishabht.com/notes/residual-denoising/): October 16, 2026. Derives how an action-space residual changes a sampled action chunk and how a denoiser residual changes the score and sampling dynamics. Discusses training, preservation of existing skills, and practical tradeoffs for robot coordination.
- [Bias and Convergence in Gradient-Clipped SGD](https://rishabht.com/notes/gradient-clipping/): September 25, 2026. Shows how clipping an unbiased stochastic gradient can reverse its expected direction, create a biased fixed point, and behave differently when gradients are averaged before or after clipping.
